 Order

The application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 ( 'BNSS'
for short) for an order of pre-arrest bail.

2. The petitioners are the accused 1 and 2 in Crime No.664/2024 of the Thaliparamba Police Station, Kannur, which is registered against the accused persons for allegedly committing the offence punishable under Section 420 read with Sec.34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The prosecution case, in brief, is that: the accused 1 to 3, in furtherance of their common intention to cheat the de facto complainant had induced him to join a Company named AAMSHE Technology on the assurance of 2024:KER:75526 BAIL APPL. NO. 6737 OF 2024 giving him good dividend.
Accordingly, the de facto complainant invested Rs.25/- Lakh between 11.11.2021 and 21.3.2022.
However, the accused did not pay any dividend and refused to pay Rs.6,05,000/- towards the salary of the daughter of the de facto complainant.
Thus, the accused have committed the above offences.

4. Heard; Sri.P.U Shailajan, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, Sri.Ajith Murali, the learned counsel appearing for the third respondent/de facto complainant and Smt.M.K Pushpalatha, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners are totally innocent of the accusations levelled against them.

There is no material to substantiate that the Rajesh Nambiar vs The Station House Officer on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101670013/

sentences.text: petitioners have received any money from the third respondent.
The entire amount was paid by the third respondent to the Managing Director of the Company.
The petitioners have not received any money from the third respondent.
Therefore, 2024:KER:75526 BAIL APPL. NO. 6737 OF 2024 by no stretch of imagination can Sec.420 be attracted against the petitioners.
The petitioners are law abiding citizens without any criminal antecedents.
Therefore, the petitioners may be granted an order of pre-arrest bail.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel appearing for the third respondent vehemently opposed the application.
The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the petitioners are habitual offenders as they are involved in seven other crimes registered by different Police Stations for committing similar offences.
The petitioners had started different Companies in Kannur, Ernakulam, Thiruvananthapuram and Secunderabad, and after receiving money from the depositors, they stopped their operations.
The petitioners are the Directors of the AAMSHE Technology.
The third accused is the Managing Director of the said Company.
The petitioners were in charge of the administration and management of the abovesaid company.
The petitioners have received the proceeds of the crime.
The petitioners' 2024:KER:75526 BAIL APPL. NO. 6737 OF 2024 custodial interrogation is necessary and recovery is to be effected.
Therefore, the application may be dismissed.

7. The prosecution allegation against the petitioners is that, the petitioners along with the third accused had induced the de facto complainant to invest money in their Company on the assurance of giving him good dividend .

Consequently, they received Rs.25/- Lakh from the de facto complainant,
but they failed to pay any dividend and the salary of the de facto complainant's daughter.
Prima facie on going through the materials on record, it is evident that there are several cases registered against the first petitioner.
It is also evident that the petitioners are Directors of the AAMSHE Technology.
The materials also show that the de facto complainant had transferred Rs.25/- Lakh to the bank account of the AAMSHE Technology.
Therefore, prima facie there is materials to show the petitioners' involvement in the crime.

8. In Jagan Mohan Reddy Y.S. v. Central 2024:KER:75526 BAIL APPL. NO. 6737 OF 2024 Bureau of Investigation [2013 KHC 4402] case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically declared that economic offences constitute a separate class and need to be visited with a different approach when it comes to the question of bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The economic offences having deep-rooted conspiracies and involving huge loss of public funds need to be viewed seriously and be considered as grave offences affecting the country's economy as a whole.

9. In Himanshu Chandravadan Desai and others v. State of Gujarat [2006 (2) SCC (Cri) 143] the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that the Courts should be circumspect and cautious in granting aniticipatory bail in crimes involving a conspiracy to cheat and defraud public institution in a systematic manner.

sentences.text: Ordinarily, arrest is a part of procedure of the investigation to secure not only the presence of the accused but several other purposes.
Power under 2024:KER:75526 BAIL APPL. NO. 6737 OF 2024 Section 438 CrPC is an extraordinary power and the same has to be exercised sparingly.
The privilege of the prearrest bail should be granted only in exceptional cases.

The judicial discretion conferred upon the court has to be properly exercised after application of mind as to the nature and gravity of the accusation; possibility of the applicant fleeing justice and other factors to decide whether it is a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail.
Grant of anticipatory bail to some extent interferes in the sphere of investigation of an offence and hence, the court must be circumspect while exercising such power for grant of anticipatory bail.

Anticipatory bail is not to be granted as a matter of rule and it has to be granted only when the court is convinced that exceptional circumstances exist to resort to that extraordinary remedy."
11.
In Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar and another, [(2012) 4 SCC 379]

entities.text: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar and another, [(2012) 4 SCC 379]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Hon'ble Supreme Court has reiterated the legal position that, an order of pre- arrest bail being an extra ordinary privilege, should be granted only in exceptional cases.
The judicial discretion conferred upon the Courts has to be properly exercised, after proper application of mind, to decide whether it is a fit case to grant an order of pre-arrest bail.
The court has to be prima facie satisfied that the applicant has been 2024:KER:75526 BAIL APPL. NO. 6737 OF 2024 falsely enroped in the crime and his liberty is being misused.

12. On an overall consideration of the facts, the rival submissions made across the Bar and the materials placed on record, and on prima facie finding that the petitioners are the Directors of the Company that received the money from the de facto complainant, the petitioners are persons with criminal antecedents, there are three cases pending before this Court for a similar relief, that the petitioners' custodial interrogation is necessary and recovery is to be effected, I am not satisfied that the petitioners have made out any valid ground to invoke the discretionary jurisdiction of this Court under Sec.482 of the BNSS.
Hence, I hold that the application is meritless and is only to be dismissed.
Resultantly, the bail application is dismissed.
